title: Normalized functional-equation sign
statement:
Let $p$ be prime, let $a\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$, and let
$q=p^a$ be the fixed prime power.
Fix $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ and an indeterminate $T$. For each integer
$i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$, let $P_i(T)\in\mathbf Z[T]$ satisfy
$P_i(0)=1$, put $b_i=\deg P_i$, and define the
determinant constant

$$
D_i=(-1)^{b_i}[T^{b_i}]P_i(T).
$$

Set

$$
\chi=\sum_{i=0}^{2d}(-1)^ib_i,
\qquad
\Delta=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}D_i^{(-1)^i}.
$$

Assume $d\chi$ is even; in geometric applications this follows from the
duality relations $b_i=b_{2d-i}$, $D_iD_{2d-i}=q^{db_i}$, and the
evenness of the middle degree when $d$ is odd. Define

$$
h=\frac{d\chi}{2}\in\mathbf Z
$$

and

$$
\varepsilon=
(-1)^\chi q^{-h}\Delta
\in\mathbf Q^\times.
$$

Negative exponents in $\Delta$ denote multiplicative inverses in
$\mathbf Q^\times$.

split_report.summary: Definition; no Lean on either branch (the only related declaration in the sources, AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.eulerChar on slopmaster2, is the coherent-sheaf Euler characteristic and not this object). Statement kept verbatim: it is the master text. Checked against the slopmaster2 LaTeX (def:functional-equation-sign, lines 3500-3519, which defines ε for a smooth-proper datum from def:euler-characteristic, def:determinant-constants and prop:functional-equation-parity, source 'Lecture 49, Definition 17.4'), against its three users (prop-functional-equation, thm-weil-final-functional-equation, thm-weil-final), which all write ε = (-1)^χ q^{-dχ/2} ∏ D_i^{(-1)^i}, against Milne LEC v2.21 Theorem 27.12 and Remark 27.13 (functional equation with exponent dχ/2 and sign ±1), and on X_0 = P^1 (b = (1,0,1), χ = 2, Δ = q, ε = 1, Z(1/(qT)) = qT^2 Z(T)). Notions named: the fixed prime power q (def-weil-finite-field-fiber, kept); the determinant constants D_i, the Euler characteristic χ and the alternating determinant scalar Δ (def-weil-determinant-constants, kept; the statement recomputes them for arbitrary P_i in Z[T] with P_i(0)=1, so it is more general than that node, whose P_i are the integral Frobenius factors); the hypothesis that dχ is even, which the remark in the statement asserts for the geometric data from the duality relations: that assertion is the hidden argument, now the new statement node prop-weil-functional-equation-parity (slopmaster2's prop:functional-equation-parity), added as a statement dependency so that h = dχ/2 is an integer for the data of the users. Everything else the statement uses is a Mathlib primitive (polynomial degree, coefficient and leading coefficient; Even; integer halving; zpow, Units and Finset.prod in ℚ), recorded in mathlib_searches rather than as leaf nodes. Mathlib has no zeta function of a variety, no Frobenius eigenvalues and no such sign: no match.
